newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT forms global postal group TNT.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT forms global postal group TNT.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Wednesday it was merging TNT Ltd, GD Express Worldwide and parts of PTT Post in a global express transport and business post company under the TNT brand name.

Ad Scheepbouwer, currently head of PTT Post, will be chief executive officer of TNT, which will employ over 50,000 people in more than 200 countries and have a turnover of some nine billion guilders in 1997, KPN and TNT said in a statement.
TNT will comprise seven business units which will all focus on offering high-quality services to their customers in several submarkets, the statement said.

"The synergies between TNT Ltd, GD Express Worldwide and PTT Post that we had foreseen at the time of the takeover, indeed exist. We consider this announcement of the new organization as the first in a row of steps toward the ideal structure for the company." Scheepbouwer said.
He said he expected the evaluation of non-core activities to be finalised in the course of this year, adding the state of affairs would be presented at the end of August.
KPN and PTT Post acquired TNT Ltd at the end of 1996 after a 2.7 billion guilder public bid for the Australian transport firm.
GD Express is an international express distribution company, jointly owned by KPN's subsidiaries TNT Ltd and GD Net.
